headline: Robinhood sets fees for its KPI binary options from Jan 1, 2027: up to 3 cents a contract, 6% of a 50-cent bet
tldr: Robinhood's earnings-metric contracts are free only through Dec 31, 2026. From Jan 1 a fee formula kicks in: 3 cents on a 50-cent contract without Gold, 1.75 cents with it.
who: Robinhood customers who trade KPI binary options, the Cboe-listed yes/no contracts that pay $1 if a company's reported metric (like EPS or revenue) hits a strike; cheap long-shot contracts are hit hardest as a share of what you pay
seo_title: Robinhood KPI binary options fees from Jan 1, 2027: the formula explained
seo_desc: Robinhood's fee schedule now says KPI binary options are $0 through Dec 31, 2026, then charge a contract fee of 10% (5% with Gold) and an exchange fee of 2% times p(1-p) per contract. Worked examples inside.

redline.after: Contract Fee: $0 through December 31, 2026 Effective January 1, 2027 Total Contract Fee = (k × p × (1 − p) × c)
redline.label: Fee Schedule · KPI Binary Options · Contract Fee
redline.note: The launch promo has an end date, and the price after it is now in writing.

redline.after: k = 10% without a Robinhood Gold subscription ● k = 5% with a Robinhood Gold subscription
redline.label: Fee Schedule · KPI Binary Options · Contract Fee rate
redline.note: Gold members pay half the Robinhood contract fee.

redline.after: Total Exchange Fee = (k × p × (1 − p) × c) k = tier-based constant ● k = 2% ● k = 5% for “Professional” orders
redline.label: Fee Schedule · KPI Binary Options · Exchange Fee
redline.note: A second, exchange fee stacks on top, and both are rounded up to the next cent.

actions: If you trade KPI binary options, note that the fee-free period ends Dec 31, 2026
Before placing an order in 2027, work out the fee: multiply 12% (7% with Gold) by p × (1 − p) by the number of contracts, where p is the price in dollars
Check the current fee schedule at cdn.robinhood.com (RHF Fee Schedule PDF) before trading, since Robinhood says regulatory fees can change without notice
what:
Robinhood Financial's fee schedule, revised Nov 10, 2026 (the PDF's own timestamp), adds a new row for KPI Binary Options, the yes/no contracts Cboe lists on company metrics such as earnings per share, revenue or a company's subscriber count. Each contract pays $1 if the reported figure meets the strike and nothing if it doesn't, so its price p sits between $0 and $1.

Change 1: The fees are free only for now. Both the exchange fee and Robinhood's contract fee read "$0 through December 31, 2026", followed by "Effective January 1, 2027" and a formula.

Change 2: The formula. Robinhood's Contract Fee is k × p × (1 − p) × c, with "k = 10% without a Robinhood Gold subscription" and "k = 5% with a Robinhood Gold subscription". The Exchange Fee uses the same formula with "k = 2%" ("k = 5% for 'Professional' orders"). Both are "rounded up to the nearest $0.01 increment". The contracts are also subject to the Regulatory Fee, Trading Activity Fee and CAT fee, with the CAT fee "reduced to 1/100 of the standard rate".

## What that means in dollars

Our arithmetic from the published formula, before the small regulatory fees: 100 contracts at 50 cents cost $50; from Jan 1 that order would carry a $2.50 contract fee plus a $0.50 exchange fee, $3.00 in total, or 6% of the stake ($1.75, or 3.5%, with Gold). Because p × (1 − p) shrinks more slowly than the price, cheap long shots pay more as a share of the stake: 100 contracts at 10 cents ($10) would carry $0.90 + $0.18 = $1.08, about 10.8%. At 90 cents the same $1.08 is about 1.2% of the $90 stake. The most any single contract can cost without Gold is 3 cents, at a 50-cent price.

What stays the same: Stock and ETF trades stay commission-free, and the footnote says the $0.50-per-contract "Professional" options fee "does not apply to KPI Binary Options"; professional orders pay the 5% exchange-fee rate instead.

The rest of today's fee-schedule diff was the PDF's layout being reflowed; the transfer, wire, margin and debit card fees read the same as before.
sources: Cboe and Robinhood announce planned launch of KPI contracts (Sep 30, 2026)
faq: Are Robinhood KPI binary options free?
Through December 31, 2026, yes: the fee schedule lists the exchange fee and contract fee as $0 until then. From January 1, 2027 both follow the formula k × p × (1 − p) × contracts.
How much will a KPI binary option cost to trade in 2027?
Without Gold, up to 3 cents per contract (at a 50-cent price) plus small regulatory fees; with Gold, up to 1.75 cents. On 100 contracts at 50 cents that's $3.00 without Gold or $1.75 with it.
Does Robinhood Gold lower the fee?
Yes. Robinhood's contract fee uses k = 5% with Gold instead of 10%; the 2% exchange fee is the same.

headline: Xbox Game Pass fine print: promo subscribers may not get Fortnite Crew benefits
tldr: Xbox's Game Pass page now warns that some perks, including Fortnite Crew benefits, aren't available during a promotional period, and says a payment method rather than a credit card is required.
who: People signing up for Xbox Game Pass on a trial or promotional price, especially for the Fortnite Crew perk

redline.after: Some experiences not available during the promotional period, including Fortnite Crew benefits.
redline.label: Game Pass · Fine print
redline.note: A new carve-out: a discounted start may not include every advertised perk.

redline.before: Offers available in select regions only. Credit card required. After promotional period, subscription automatically continues at the then-current regular price (subject to change), unless canceled, plus applicable taxes.
redline.after: Offers are available for a limited time in select regions only. Valid payment method required. After promotional period, subscription automatically continues at the then-current regular price unless canceled.
redline.label: Game Pass · Promotional Offers

actions: If you're joining Game Pass on a promo for Fortnite Crew, confirm the benefit is included before you pay
Set a reminder before the promotional period ends; the subscription still renews at the regular price unless you cancel
what: The fine print on Xbox's Game Pass page was rewritten. A new line says "Some experiences not available during the promotional period, including Fortnite Crew benefits." The promotional-offer terms now say "Valid payment method required" instead of "Credit card required", and "Eligibility varies by offer; some offers are for new subscribers only." The renewal sentence still says the subscription "automatically continues at the then-current regular price unless canceled"; the words "(subject to change)" and "plus applicable taxes" were dropped from it. The subscription terms link moved from xbox.com/subscriptionterms to xbox.com/terms, now labeled "XBOX Subscription and Cloud Terms". Other edits trimmed the Rewards and gift card footnotes and reordered menu links.

headline: Audible's plan page drops the 'don't roll over' warning and lists its $229.50 plan as 12 credits
tldr: Audible's Standard plan card no longer says unused monthly picks don't roll over, and the $229.50-a-year Premium card now reads "12 creditos/año" where it said 24 audiobooks.
who: People comparing Audible's Standard and annual Premium plans before signing up

redline.before: Auto-renews at $8.99/mo after 30 days. Cancel anytime. Unused monthly audiobook selections don't roll over.
redline.after: Auto-renews at $8.99/mo after 30 days. Cancel anytime.
redline.label: Pricing · Standard
redline.note: The roll-over warning added Oct 23 is gone from the card; the FAQ still says Standard is 1 audiobook a month.

redline.label: Pricing · Premium Annual, $229.50/yr
redline.note: A Spanish label showing 12 credits on the plan that offered 24; it may be a page error, so check checkout.

actions: If you're buying the $229.50 annual Premium plan, confirm at checkout how many credits it includes before paying
what: Audible's member-benefits page changed its plan cards again. The Standard card dropped "Unused monthly audiobook selections don't roll over", the line we logged being added on Oct 23; the FAQ still describes Standard as selecting 1 audiobook a month. The two annual Premium cards now read "12 audiobooks" at "$149.50 a year" and, for the $229.50 plan, "12 creditos/año" (Spanish for 12 credits a year) with "Save 16%", where yesterday it said "24 audiobooks". The page doesn't explain the change, and the Spanish wording suggests a labeling error rather than a new allowance, so we'd treat the 24-credit plan as unconfirmed until Audible's checkout says otherwise. The headline also changed from "Access our 1M+ catalog with membership" to "Choose the plan that's right for you", and the monthly cards now say "30-day free trial".
